meta.disclaimer: Descriptive text in this dataset is a structured demonstration dataset prepared for judge-education and consultation purposes. It paraphrases general morphological and functional expectations and is NOT a verbatim reproduction of any official WDF breed standard. Always verify against the official source standard before using in examination or judging contexts.

breeds.group: Group 1 Shepherd Dogs and Cattle Dogs

identity.historical_function: Livestock guardian of the Carpathian mountains, protecting flocks against large predators such as wolves and bears over long working days in harsh terrain.
identity.general_impression: A large, rustic and well-proportioned livestock guardian, powerful without heaviness, showing calm confidence and natural robustness adapted to mountain work.
identity.important_proportions: Slightly longer than tall; depth of chest reaching approximately to the elbow; balanced, functional proportions favouring endurance over exaggeration.
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Clearly expressed. Males are larger, heavier-boned and more masculine in head; females are somewhat lighter and more refined while remaining substantial.
identity.ideal_type_summary: A functional mountain guardian: substantial bone, weather-resistant double coat, sober expression and steady temperament suited to independent guarding.

anatomy.head: Moderately broad, in proportion to the body, wolf-like in overall aspect without coarseness.
anatomy.skull: Slightly domed, broad between the ears, tapering gradually toward the muzzle.
anatomy.muzzle: Strong and deep, tapering slightly, roughly equal to or slightly shorter than the skull length.
anatomy.jaws_teeth: Strong jaws with a complete scissor bite; full, well-developed dentition preferred.
anatomy.eyes: Medium, almond-shaped, obliquely set, dark brown, with a calm and attentive expression.
anatomy.ears: Set at or slightly above eye level, V-shaped, dropping close to the cheeks.
anatomy.neck: Strong, muscular, of moderate length, carried without exaggerated dewlap.
anatomy.topline: Firm and level, with a well-muscled back.
anatomy.body: Robust and slightly elongated, with good substance and no lightness.
anatomy.chest: Deep and long, reaching to the elbow, ribs well sprung but not barrel-shaped.
anatomy.tail: Set moderately high, hanging when at rest, raised to back level or slightly above in action, never curled over the back.
anatomy.forequarters: Straight, strong-boned, well-angulated shoulders, upright and parallel when viewed from the front.
anatomy.hindquarters: Muscular with moderate, functional angulation providing drive and endurance.
anatomy.feet: Oval, compact, with strong pads and well-arched toes.
anatomy.movement: Free, balanced and enduring; a supple, ground-covering trot typical of a working mountain dog.
anatomy.coat: Double coat with a dense undercoat and a harsh, straight, weather-resistant outer coat; longer on the neck, back of the legs and tail.
anatomy.color: Typically a background of sandy-grey to fawn with darker overlay; clear defined markings and overall harmony are valued.

temperament.behavior: Calm, balanced and devoted to the flock and family; naturally suspicious of strangers without unprovoked aggression.
temperament.ring_attitude: Self-assured and steady; may show independence but should accept examination without nervousness.
temperament.temperament_notes: An independent decision-maker bred to work without constant handler guidance; stability under pressure is essential.

disqualifying: Tail curled tightly over the back

frequent_confusions: May be confused with the Ciobănesc Românesc Mioritic, which is longer-coated and lighter in colour
Confused with other large mountain guardians by novice students
key_markers: Weather-resistant double coat with darker overlay
judge_notes: Reward functional working type over size alone
Check for stable temperament during static examination
teaching_notes: Use alongside the Mioritic to teach coat and colour distinctions
Emphasise the working-guardian purpose behind the standard

movement_exam: Efficiency and endurance of the trot

breeds.internal_notes: Demo entry. Text paraphrases general expectations for a Carpathian-type livestock guardian; confirm official WDF wording before teaching use.
recurring_judge_observations: Confused with the Mioritic — check coat length and colour first

breeds.group: Group 1 Shepherd Dogs and Cattle Dogs

identity.historical_function: Originally a herding and flock-tending dog, later developed into a versatile working dog for service, protection and utility roles.
identity.general_impression: A medium-to-large, slightly elongated, powerful and well-muscled dog with dry bone and firm overall structure conveying agility and endurance.
identity.important_proportions: Length exceeds height at withers by roughly 10–17%; body clearly longer than tall, with harmonious transitions.
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Distinct; males are visibly more masculine and larger, females more feminine, each unmistakable in secondary sex characteristics.
identity.ideal_type_summary: A balanced, agile working dog with strong nerves, correct angulation and effortless, far-reaching trot.

anatomy.head: Wedge-shaped, clean-cut, proportional to the body, moderately broad between the ears.
anatomy.muzzle: Strong, wedge-shaped, with a straight nasal bridge; roughly half the total head length.
anatomy.jaws_teeth: Powerful jaws, complete scissor bite with 42 teeth; full dentition strongly preferred.
anatomy.eyes: Almond-shaped, medium, dark, set slightly obliquely, with a lively and confident expression.
anatomy.ears: Erect, medium, carried upright and parallel, pointing forward.
anatomy.neck: Strong, well-muscled, without excessive dewlap, carried at about 45 degrees at ease.
anatomy.topline: Runs from neck over well-defined withers into a straight back and a gently sloping croup, without visible interruption.
anatomy.body: Slightly elongated, deep and firm, well-muscled.
anatomy.chest: Moderately broad, long and deep, reaching to the elbow, with well-carried ribs.
anatomy.tail: Bushy, reaching at least to the hock, hanging in a slight curve at rest, raised in action but not above the back level.
anatomy.forequarters: Shoulder blade and upper arm well-angled, of equal length, firmly attached; legs straight and dry.
anatomy.hindquarters: Broad and well-muscled thighs with correct angulation providing powerful, elastic drive.
anatomy.feet: Rounded, compact, well-arched toes; hard pads, dark nails.
anatomy.movement: A far-reaching, ground-covering trot with powerful drive and free reach; topline remains firm and steady.
anatomy.coat: Double coat with dense straight harsh close-lying outer coat and thick undercoat (standard stock-coat variety).
anatomy.color: Black-and-tan, black-and-red, sable, or solid black; masks and saddle patterns common. Pale washed-out colours undesirable.

temperament.behavior: Balanced, self-assured, confident and trainable; steady nerves and controlled trainability with strong working drive.
temperament.ring_attitude: Attentive and composed, accepting examination readily.
temperament.temperament_notes: Nerve stability, confidence and controlled drive are core; timidity or unwarranted aggression are serious departures.

minor: Minor deviation in ear carriage in young dogs
disqualifying: Overshot or undershot bite, missing multiple teeth
Hanging or non-erect ears in an adult

frequent_confusions: Working-line vs show-line type variation confuses students
Long-stock-coat variety mistaken for a separate breed
judge_notes: Assess movement as the defining functional test
Do not reward exaggerated rear angulation that compromises soundness
teaching_notes: Use gait analysis to teach reach and drive
Discuss type divergence between lines objectively

movement_exam: Reach and drive at the trot

breeds.internal_notes: Demo entry. Paraphrased general expectations; verify against official WDF wording, especially dentition and proportion figures.
recurring_judge_observations: Watch for over-angulated rear masking unsoundness

breeds.group: Group 1 Shepherd Dogs and Cattle Dogs

identity.historical_function: Developed to drove cattle over vast distances by heeling; a hardy, agile working dog for demanding stock conditions.
identity.general_impression: A compact, symmetrical working dog with substance, agility and great endurance; the very picture of a hard-working heeler.
identity.important_proportions: Slightly longer than tall (length to height roughly 10:9); strong and sturdy without heaviness.
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Moderate; males more robust, females somewhat finer, both retaining working substance.
identity.ideal_type_summary: A muscular, agile and tireless cattle-driving dog, alert and ready for action.

anatomy.head: Strong, in balance with the body, broad skull curving slightly between the ears.
anatomy.skull: Broad and slightly curved, flat between the ears.
anatomy.muzzle: Broad, well-filled under the eyes, tapering to a medium length, powerful.
anatomy.jaws_teeth: Strong jaws, sound even scissor bite; teeth strong and well-spaced.
anatomy.eyes: Oval, medium, dark brown, with an alert and wary expression.
anatomy.ears: Moderately small, pricked, set wide apart, thick and pointed.
anatomy.neck: Very strong, muscular, of medium length, broadening to the shoulders.
anatomy.topline: Level and firm with a strong, muscular back.
anatomy.body: Compact, deep, with well-sprung ribs and strong loin.
anatomy.chest: Deep and muscular, of moderate breadth, reaching to the elbow.
anatomy.tail: Set moderately low, hanging in a slight curve at rest, with a good brush; not carried over the back.
anatomy.forequarters: Strong round bone, sloping shoulders, straight parallel legs.
anatomy.hindquarters: Broad, strong, muscular thighs with well-turned stifle and strong hocks.
anatomy.feet: Round, short, well-arched toes, strong pads and short nails.
anatomy.movement: Free, supple and tireless, with sound reach and drive; capable of quick, sudden movement typical of a working heeler.
anatomy.coat: Smooth double coat with short dense undercoat and a moderately short, straight, weather-resistant outer coat.
anatomy.color: Blue or red speckle; blue may show black, blue or tan markings; red speckle evenly distributed. Symmetrical head markings valued.

temperament.behavior: Alert, courageous, intensely loyal and protective; naturally wary of strangers.
temperament.ring_attitude: Watchful and businesslike; should tolerate examination without aggression.
temperament.temperament_notes: Extreme working drive; suspicion of strangers is typical but must not become uncontrolled aggression.

disqualifying: Coat markedly incorrect in type or colour

frequent_confusions: Confused with the Australian Stumpy Tail Cattle Dog (tailless variety)
Blue colour confused with merle patterning by beginners
judge_notes: Assess for working soundness and agility
Check even colour distribution and symmetrical head markings
teaching_notes: Explain speckle vs merle to prevent confusion
Relate build to the heeling function

breeds.internal_notes: Demo entry. Colour genetics note (speckle vs merle) added for teaching; verify official colour wording.
recurring_judge_observations: Verify even speckling and symmetrical head markings

breeds.group: Group 2 Pinscher and Schnauzer Type Dogs – Molossoids and Swiss Cattle Dogs

identity.historical_function: A driving and draught dog for cattle and butchers, later used as a service, protection and working dog.
identity.general_impression: A robust, powerful and above-medium-sized dog, neither heavy nor light, with substantial bone and strong musculature conveying strength and endurance.
identity.important_proportions: Length of body to height at withers should not exceed roughly 15:10; compact and powerful outline.
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Pronounced; males clearly larger, heavier-boned and broader in head, females distinctly feminine while remaining substantial.
identity.ideal_type_summary: A calm, powerful molossoid-type working dog of great strength, courage and self-assured steadiness.

anatomy.head: Medium length, broad between the ears; forehead moderately arched in profile.
anatomy.skull: Broad, with well-developed but not over-pronounced zygomatic arches.
anatomy.muzzle: Deep, broad at the base, slightly tapering; nasal bridge broad and straight, roughly proportionate to the skull.
anatomy.jaws_teeth: Strong, complete scissor bite with 42 teeth; powerful jaws.
anatomy.eyes: Almond-shaped, medium, dark brown, with a good-natured, confident and alert expression.
anatomy.ears: Medium, pendant, triangular, set high and wide, lying flat against the head.
anatomy.neck: Strong, well-muscled, moderately long, slightly arched, free from excessive dewlap.
anatomy.body: Compact and powerful, with broad deep chest and strong loin.
anatomy.chest: Roomy, broad and deep, reaching to the elbow, with well-sprung ribs.
anatomy.tail: In natural condition carried level in extension of the topline; may hang at rest.
anatomy.forequarters: Strongly boned, straight, well-muscled; sloping long shoulder blade.
anatomy.hindquarters: Long, broad, strongly muscled thighs with sound angulation and powerful drive.
anatomy.feet: Round, compact, well-arched toes; hard pads, strong dark nails.
anatomy.movement: A trotting dog; movement harmonious, steady, full of energy, with good reach in front and powerful drive behind, topline remaining firm.
anatomy.coat: Double coat with medium-harsh, dense, flat top coat and undercoat, undercoat not showing through.
anatomy.color: Black with clearly defined mahogany to rich tan markings in the prescribed pattern.

temperament.behavior: Good-natured, placid, devoted, obedient and self-assured; steady and courageous.
temperament.ring_attitude: Calm and confident; should accept handling without nervousness or aggression.
temperament.temperament_notes: Self-assured steadiness is the hallmark; nervousness, timidity or indiscriminate aggression are serious faults.

minor: Tan markings slightly too extensive or diffuse
disqualifying: Ground colour other than black; absence of the tan pattern

frequent_confusions: Confused with other black-and-tan molossoid or working types by beginners
Overweight specimens mistaken for correct substance
key_markers: Broad powerful head with defined stop
Black coat with clean mahogany markings
judge_notes: Reward correct substance, not exaggerated mass
Verify the tan-marking pattern and clean boundaries
teaching_notes: Distinguish substance from overweight
Use the marking pattern as a teaching landmark

movement_exam: Reach and drive at the trot

breeds.internal_notes: Demo entry. Emphasis on substance-vs-overweight distinction for teaching. Verify official marking description.
recurring_judge_observations: Distinguish correct substance from overweight condition

breeds.group: Group 2 Pinscher and Schnauzer Type Dogs – Molossoids and Swiss Cattle Dogs

identity.historical_function: Developed as a protection, companion and working dog; a refined, elegant guard dog of medium size.
identity.general_impression: A medium-sized, muscular and elegantly built dog of noble appearance, with clean lines conveying nobility, temperament and endurance.
identity.important_proportions: Nearly square; length of body only slightly exceeds height at withers (roughly 5% in males, 10% in females).
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Clear; males more masculine and substantial, females more refined, both athletic and elegant.
identity.ideal_type_summary: An elegant, athletic and alert working dog with dry muscle, clean outline and lively temperament.

anatomy.head: Strong, in proportion, resembling a blunt wedge from both front and side.
anatomy.skull: Flat top, developing in a straight line toward the muzzle; slight furrow.
anatomy.muzzle: Deep, well-developed, with wide upper and lower jaws; roughly balanced with the skull.
anatomy.jaws_teeth: Strong deep jaws, complete scissor bite with 42 teeth set perpendicularly.
anatomy.eyes: Medium, oval, dark, with a lively, alert and energetic expression.
anatomy.ears: Set high; in the natural, undocked form dropped and lying close to the cheeks.
anatomy.neck: Fairly long, lean, muscular, rising well from the shoulders, slightly arched, dry.
anatomy.topline: Descends slightly from a well-developed wither to a short firm back and short croup.
anatomy.body: Compact, square and muscular, with well-developed forechest.
anatomy.chest: Moderately broad, deep, reaching to the elbow, with well-sprung ribs.
anatomy.tail: In the natural form carried as a slight continuation of the topline, moderately high set.
anatomy.forequarters: Sloping shoulder blade, well-angled, dry and muscular; straight strong-boned legs.
anatomy.hindquarters: Broad muscular thighs with sound angulation delivering powerful, elastic drive.
anatomy.feet: Short, arched, compact (cat-like), with dark nails.
anatomy.movement: Elegant, free, elastic and ground-covering; front reaches well forward, rear drives powerfully, topline firm.
anatomy.coat: Short, hard, thick and close-lying, smooth and evenly covering the body, without undercoat.
anatomy.color: Black or brown, in each case with clearly defined rust-red markings in the prescribed pattern.

temperament.behavior: Friendly, calm, strongly bonded to family, alert and courageous with moderate, controllable sharpness.
temperament.ring_attitude: Alert and confident; should accept examination without nervousness.
temperament.temperament_notes: Balance of alertness, courage and controllability is essential; anxiety or excessive sharpness are faults.

disqualifying: White markings or incorrect ground colour

frequent_confusions: Confused with the Rottweiler by colour pattern despite very different type
Manchester Terrier confused as a smaller similar type
key_markers: Short close coat with sharp rust markings
judge_notes: Assess elegance combined with substance and dry muscle
Verify square proportions and marking definition
teaching_notes: Contrast with Rottweiler to teach type vs colour
Use outline to teach 'square' proportion

breeds.internal_notes: Demo entry. Natural (undocked) ears and tail described; verify official presentation requirements.
recurring_judge_observations: Confirm square proportions and clean marking boundaries

identity.historical_function: A working earth terrier bred to bolt fox and go to ground; compact, agile and fearless below ground.
identity.general_impression: A strong, active, lithe working terrier of great character with a flexible body of medium length, presenting a lively, alert workmanlike outline.
identity.important_proportions: Slightly longer than tall; overall balance and a chest spannable by average-sized hands are essential working features.
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Modest; males slightly stronger, females somewhat finer, both retaining a workmanlike build.
identity.ideal_type_summary: A compact, spannable working earth terrier: agile, fearless and functionally built for going to ground.

anatomy.head: Flat skull of moderate width, gradually decreasing toward the eyes.
anatomy.muzzle: Powerful, well-boned, of good depth; length from stop to nose slightly shorter than skull.
anatomy.jaws_teeth: Strong jaws, muscular cheeks, complete scissor bite with strong teeth.
anatomy.eyes: Small, dark, almond-shaped, keen, with a lively expression; not prominent.
anatomy.ears: Button or dropped, of good texture and great mobility, carried close to the head.
anatomy.neck: Strong and clean, of good length, allowing the head to be carried with poise.
anatomy.body: Rectangular, of medium length, with flexible loin and a chest that can be spanned behind the shoulders.
anatomy.chest: Depth from withers to brisket does not exceed distance from brisket to ground; chest deep rather than wide, spannable.
anatomy.tail: In the natural form set high and carried gaily; provides a good handhold in working type.
anatomy.forequarters: Straight-boned legs, shoulders well laid back and sloping, elbows close to the body.
anatomy.hindquarters: Strong, muscular, with good angulation and parallel hocks giving effortless drive.
anatomy.feet: Round, hard-padded, neither turning in nor out, with moderately arched toes.
anatomy.movement: True, free and springy, with good reach and drive; straight coming and going.
anatomy.coat: Smooth, broken or rough, all weatherproof; must be dense and provide protection, skin thick and loose.
anatomy.color: Predominantly white with black, tan or tan-and-black markings; markings preferably confined to the head and root of tail.

temperament.behavior: Bold, fearless, friendly and confident; a keen, tireless working attitude.
temperament.ring_attitude: Alert and lively; should show confidence and accept examination.
temperament.expression: Keen, intelligent and full of life.
temperament.temperament_notes: Working boldness is essential; the dog should be spirited but not uncontrollably aggressive.

disqualifying: Complete absence of white / incorrect ground colour

frequent_confusions: Confused with the Parson Russell Terrier, which is taller and squarer
Confused with smooth Fox Terrier lines
key_markers: Spannable chest as a working test
Predominantly white coat with restricted markings
judge_notes: Physically span the chest as a functional check
Value working balance over showiness
teaching_notes: Demonstrate the chest-span test
Contrast proportions with the Parson Russell

breeds.internal_notes: Demo entry. Chest-span working test highlighted for teaching. Verify official height and proportion figures.
recurring_judge_observations: Physically span the chest as a working check

identity.historical_function: Developed from bull-and-terrier stock into a powerful, agile companion and utility dog of the bull type.
identity.general_impression: A stocky, muscular yet agile dog giving the impression of great strength for its size; well put together, neither leggy nor low.
identity.important_proportions: Height and weight in proportion; body a little longer than tall; substantial without cloddiness.
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Marked; males broader in head and heavier-boned, females feminine but powerful.
identity.ideal_type_summary: A powerful, agile bull-type dog combining muscle and balance with a confident, good-natured character.

anatomy.head: Medium length, deep through, broad skull with very pronounced cheek muscles.
anatomy.muzzle: Medium length, rounded on the upper side, dropping abruptly below the eyes; well-developed jaws.
anatomy.jaws_teeth: Powerful jaws with strong under-jaw; scissor bite, teeth strong and even.
anatomy.eyes: Round, dark, low and wide apart, giving an alert intelligent expression.
anatomy.ears: Set high; in the natural form rose or half-pricked, carried close.
anatomy.neck: Heavy, slightly arched, muscular, tapering from shoulders to the back of the skull, no looseness of skin.
anatomy.body: Compact and muscular, deep-chested with well-sprung ribs and a well-tucked loin.
anatomy.chest: Deep and broad, reaching approximately to the elbow, forelegs set rather wide apart.
anatomy.tail: Short in comparison to size, set low, tapering to a fine point, not curled or carried over the back.
anatomy.forequarters: Heavy-boned, straight legs, large muscular shoulders held firmly.
anatomy.hindquarters: Well-muscled, let down at the hocks, turning neither in nor out.
anatomy.movement: Springy, effortless and agile, without rolling or pacing; strong drive with balanced reach.
anatomy.coat: Short, close, stiff to the touch and glossy.
anatomy.color: All colours, solid, parti or patched are permissible; predominantly white or largely black-and-tan are less favoured.

temperament.behavior: Confident, courageous, good-natured and attentive; strongly attached to people.
temperament.ring_attitude: Bold and stable; should accept examination confidently.
temperament.temperament_notes: Confidence with stability is the ideal; unwarranted aggression and nervousness are both undesirable.

serious: Light bone or lack of substance

frequent_confusions: Confused with the Staffordshire Bull Terrier, which is smaller
Confused with the American Pit Bull Terrier type
key_markers: Broad head with pronounced cheek muscles
judge_notes: Assess balance of power and agility, not bulk alone
Reward confident stable temperament
teaching_notes: Compare size and proportion with the Staffordshire Bull Terrier
Discuss bull-type origins objectively

breeds.internal_notes: Demo entry. Distinction from Staffordshire Bull Terrier emphasised for teaching. Verify official colour preferences.
recurring_judge_observations: Assess balance of power and agility, not bulk alone

breeds.group: Group 5 Dogs of the Primitive Type

identity.historical_function: An ancient hunting dog of central Africa, used to drive game into nets and to track; noted for not barking in the usual way.
identity.general_impression: A lightly built, finely boned, aristocratic-looking dog, high on the leg, poised and alert, with a wrinkled forehead and tightly curled tail.
identity.important_proportions: Balanced and square in outline; height at withers approximately equal to length of body; elegant and racy.
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Subtle; males slightly stronger, females finer, both light and elegant.
identity.ideal_type_summary: An elegant, primitive-type hunting dog: square, high on the leg, alert, with a wrinkled brow and curled tail.

anatomy.head: Flat, well-chiselled, of medium width, tapering toward the nose; fine profuse wrinkles appear on the forehead when the ears are erect.
anatomy.muzzle: Shorter than the skull, tapering, neither coarse nor snipey.
anatomy.jaws_teeth: Level jaws with a perfect scissor bite; teeth even.
anatomy.eyes: Almond-shaped, dark, obliquely set, with a far-seeing, inscrutable expression.
anatomy.ears: Small, pointed, erect and slightly hooded, of fine texture, set well forward on the top of the head.
anatomy.neck: Of good length, strong, well-crested, slightly full at the base, carrying the head proudly.
anatomy.body: Short-coupled and balanced, with a defined waist; oval light bone.
anatomy.chest: Deep, of medium width, with ribs well sprung and oval.
anatomy.tail: Set high on the topline, curling tightly over to either side and lying close.
anatomy.forequarters: Straight, fine-boned legs with long forearms; shoulders well laid back.
anatomy.hindquarters: Strong and muscular with well let-down hocks, moderate angulation, long second thigh.
anatomy.feet: Small, narrow, compact, with well-arched toes and thick pads.
anatomy.movement: Swift, tireless, long-striding and effortless, resembling a racehorse trotting; legs moving in parallel planes.
anatomy.coat: Short, fine, close and dense; skin very pliant.
anatomy.color: Pure bright colours: black; red; black-and-tan; brindle; all with white feet, chest and tail tip; white legs, blaze and collar optional.

temperament.behavior: Alert, affectionate, energetic and curious; reserved with strangers, intelligent and independent.
temperament.ring_attitude: Poised and slightly aloof; should tolerate examination while remaining alert.
temperament.temperament_notes: A primitive, independent nature; reserve is typical but should not tip into fearfulness or aggression.

disqualifying: Ears not erect in an adult

frequent_confusions: Confused with other primitive spitz-like types by beginners
Wrinkle and tail curl overlooked as key markers
judge_notes: Look for the characteristic racehorse-like trot
Value elegance and correct primitive type
teaching_notes: Use as an example of primitive type and function
Point out barkless vocalisation as a breed trait (informational)

breeds.internal_notes: Demo entry. Primitive-type markers (wrinkle, curled tail) emphasised for teaching. Verify official colour and marking wording.
recurring_judge_observations: Look for wrinkle when ears erect and tight tail curl

breeds.group: Group 1 Shepherd Dogs and Cattle Dogs

identity.historical_function: A Carpathian livestock guardian bred to live with and defend flocks against large predators, working independently in harsh mountain conditions.
identity.general_impression: A large, imposing, abundantly coated livestock guardian, rustic and powerful, conveying calm strength and a shaggy, weather-hardy outline.
identity.important_proportions: Slightly longer than tall; substantial and deep-bodied, with the long coat adding to the impression of size.
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Clear; males noticeably larger, heavier-boned and more massive in head, females somewhat lighter while remaining large.
identity.ideal_type_summary: A massive, long-coated Carpathian guardian: heavy bone, dense shaggy double coat, calm confidence and independent guarding character.

anatomy.head: Not too large in proportion to the body, moderately broad, covered with abundant hair.
anatomy.skull: Slightly domed and broad, tapering gently toward the muzzle.
anatomy.muzzle: Strong, well-developed, slightly shorter than the skull, tapering but never pointed.
anatomy.jaws_teeth: Strong jaws with a complete scissor bite; well-developed dentition.
anatomy.eyes: Medium or rather small, obliquely set, dark chestnut, with a calm, confident expression, often partly hidden by hair.
anatomy.ears: Set at eye level, V-shaped, dropping close to the head, covered with long hair.
anatomy.neck: Strong, muscular, of medium length, well-covered with abundant coat.
anatomy.topline: Firm and level, with a broad, muscular back.
anatomy.body: Massive, slightly elongated, deep and substantial.
anatomy.chest: Broad, deep and long, reaching to the elbow, with well-sprung ribs.
anatomy.tail: Set on rather high, well-feathered, hanging at rest and raised to about back level in action, never tightly curled.
anatomy.forequarters: Strong-boned, straight, well-muscled, with well-laid shoulders.
anatomy.hindquarters: Broad, muscular, with moderate functional angulation providing endurance.
anatomy.feet: Oval, compact, with strong pads and well-arched toes.
anatomy.movement: Free and balanced, with good reach and drive; an enduring, ground-covering trot suited to mountain work.
anatomy.coat: Abundant double coat; profuse, long, slightly wavy outer coat with a dense undercoat, forming a shaggy, protective covering over the whole body.
anatomy.color: Whole white, or white with clearly defined grey or black patches; a uniform impression is preferred.

temperament.behavior: Calm, balanced, devoted and courageous; naturally distrustful of strangers and strongly protective of the flock.
temperament.ring_attitude: Steady and self-assured; should accept examination while remaining watchful.
temperament.temperament_notes: An independent guardian; stability and controlled protectiveness are essential, with no unwarranted aggression or nervousness.

disqualifying: Short coat, or tail tightly curled over the back

Confused with other large white or shaggy guardians

Reward functional working substance over sheer size

identity.historical_function: A pack scenthound bred to hunt hare by scent over long distances, working in company with great stamina and voice.
identity.general_impression: A sturdy, compact scenthound of quality, merry and active, conveying determination and stamina without coarseness.
identity.important_proportions: Compact and balanced; body slightly longer than tall, with strength appropriate to a working pack hound.
identity.sexual_dimorphism: Moderate; males somewhat stronger, females finer, both compact and workmanlike.
identity.ideal_type_summary: A compact, sound, merry pack scenthound built for stamina, with a good nose and clear hound character.

anatomy.head: Fairly long, powerful without coarseness, finer in the bitch, free from frown.

lessons.title: Carpatin vs. Mioritic — telling the two Romanian guardians apart
lessons.summary: A focused comparison of the two Romanian Carpathian guardians most often confused by candidates.
learning_objectives: Distinguish the Carpatin from the Mioritic by coat length and colour
Recognise the shared guardian type and independent temperament
Apply the correct recognition markers under ring conditions
lessons.body:
The Ciobănesc Românesc Carpatin and the Ciobănesc Românesc Mioritic share a common function as Carpathian livestock guardians, but differ clearly in appearance.

The Carpatin carries a shorter, weather-resistant double coat in sandy-grey to fawn with a darker overlay, and a sober wolf-like head. The Mioritic is larger in impression, with an abundant, long, shaggy double coat, typically white or white with grey/black patches.

Under ring conditions, resolve the confusion first by coat length and colour, then confirm by head type and overall substance. Reward functional working substance over sheer size in both.
recommended_reading: Comparative notes on Carpathian guardian types

lessons.title: Rottweiler and Dobermann — substance versus elegance
lessons.summary: Two German working breeds of the same group that teach the contrast between powerful substance and refined elegance.
learning_objectives: Contrast the compact powerful Rottweiler with the square elegant Dobermann
Read the black-and-tan marking pattern correctly in each
Separate correct substance from overweight condition
lessons.body:
Both breeds sit in the Pinscher/Schnauzer–Molossoid group and share a black coat with rust/tan markings, which can confuse beginners despite very different type.

The Rottweiler is robust, compact and powerful, with a broad head and defined stop. The Dobermann is nearly square, elegant and athletic, with a blunt-wedge head and dry muscle.

Teach candidates to read type before colour: marking pattern is shared, but proportion, substance and outline separate the two immediately.

lessons.title: Herding foundations — Group 1 shepherds and cattle dogs
lessons.summary: An orientation lesson on the shepherd and cattle-dog group, drawing on all Group 1 breeds in the database.
learning_objectives: Describe the functional range of Group 1 breeds
Relate structure and movement to herding and guarding work
Identify each Group 1 breed by its key markers
lessons.body:
Group 1 gathers shepherd and cattle dogs whose structure serves herding, droving or guarding. This lesson uses every Group 1 breed currently in the database so the test scales as you add more.

Focus on efficient, enduring movement and on the distinct recognition markers of each breed.
